[Previous context: A single

comprehensive structural and household status assessment would be an

powerful tool to ensure public safety (against the risk of compromised

buildings), assist with the social and economic recovery (by encouraging the

reoccupation of safe buildings), relieve trauma (by demonstrating the recovery

is starting), recovery planning (by providing the essential data to formulate and] budget recovery plans), implementation and monitoring of recovery (by linking

assessments to follow-up recovery actions by households), and promoting long-

term risk reduction (by informing the development of resilient reconstruction

practices). The Government of Nepal agreed that the Bank would lead this effort

and the DRM team is fully engaged in cooperation with Government, National

Society for Earthquake Technology-Nepal (NSET), Nepal Engineering

Association (NEA) and United Nations Office for Project Services (UNOPS),
